trends.name: CFPB Section 1033 open banking rule stayed and under re-write
trends.specificImpact: 2024 final rule guaranteeing free standardized data access was enjoined (E.D. Kentucky); CFPB opened new ANPR Aug 2025. Legal 'right to data' now uncertain and delayed — reverts to bilateral aggregator/bank commercial terms, raising integration risk/cost for aid-refund pacing feature.

trends.name: Bank data-access fees monetization (JPMorgan-Plaid deal)
trends.specificImpact: JPMorgan began charging aggregators for data access in 2025 (Plaid facing up to ~$300M/yr); other banks expected to follow. Continuous 'runway pacing' implies frequent polling — exactly the high-frequency access banks are now pricing, threatening unit economics for low-ARPU student users.

trends.name: Post-Cleo FTC enforcement on fintech subscription/claim transparency
trends.specificImpact: March 2025 $17M Cleo settlement targeted deceptive money-availability claims and hard-to-cancel subscriptions. Competitive tailwind for honest, avoidance-reducing design: discredits predatory cash-advance incumbents, rewards clear disclosure and easy cancellation from day one.

trends.name: AI financial advice governed by existing frameworks, no AI-specific rule yet
trends.specificImpact: SEC/FINRA apply existing fiduciary/disclosure law to AI; 2025 exam priorities include AI; FINRA 2026 report requires plain-English algorithm explanation. Design constraint: position as informational pacing tool, not investment advice.

trends.name: On-device / local LLMs for private financial data
trends.specificImpact: Apple's ~3B on-device model and 2026 on-device AI push make local inference on financial data viable. Unlocks privacy-differentiated positioning, lowers per-user inference cost, supports emotional/avoidance-reduction design via private, judgment-free coaching.

trends.name: Agentic AI banking assistants going mainstream
trends.specificImpact: Agentic AI in finance jumped <7% (Jan 2025) to ~44% (Q1 2026); JPMorgan/BofA (3.2B Erica interactions) ship autonomous assistants suggesting savings strategies. Incumbents embedding AI advisors in bank apps where aid refunds land threatens to close the wedge before a standalone app can differentiate.

trends.name: Gen Z acute financial anxiety and avoidance behavior
trends.specificImpact: ~70% of Gen Z report money stress disrupting sleep; insecurity rose 30%->48% (2024->2025, Deloitte); ~1 in 3 cope via avoidance instead of budgeting. Validates emotional/avoidance-reduction design thesis against high-effort incumbents like YNAB.

trends.name: Gen Z distrust of social finance content and de-influencing
trends.specificImpact: ~53% of Gen Z name TikTok least trustworthy source for financial advice yet still use it; de-influencing/demand for transparency rising. Opens door for credible, disclosure-forward brand, but AI advice must earn trust through transparency or skepticism becomes headwind.

trends.name: Student loan / aid policy upheaval (SAVE end, RAP, Pell changes, OBBBA)
trends.specificImpact: SAVE vacated (March 2026), interest resumed Aug 2025, 7.5M borrowers re-choosing plans July 2026; new RAP plan, Pell expansion, Parent PLUS caps, taxable IDR forgiveness from 2026. Aid rule churn strengthens aid-refund-pacing wedge as disbursement timing becomes more salient.

trends.name: College affordability paradox: rising sticker price, flat net price
trends.specificImpact: Sticker tuition rose 2.9-4.0% for 2025-26 but inflation-adjusted net tuition fell (public four-year ~$2,300 net); >40% consider trade/community alternatives. Strong cost anxiety (marketing tailwind) but budget-constrained TAM caps WTP — pushes toward freemium/non-subscription monetization.

trends.name: Gig/side-hustle income now central for Gen Z students
trends.specificImpact: ~58% of Gen Z workers hold a side hustle; gig income can reach ~57% of total income for some; earnings fluctuate weekly/monthly. Directly validates irregular-income modeling wedge — target user has lumpy aid disbursements plus volatile gig income, a combo incumbents built on steady salary handle poorly.

De-influencing/TikTok-trust stats largely from secondary/press citations of proprietary studies.
No direct evidence on whether campus-card/financial-aid-office disbursement systems (BankMobile/BMTX, Nelnet) expose usable APIs — critical integration dependency.
AI-advice regulatory risk inferred from adviser-focused frameworks; boundary for non-investment budgeting AI untested.
On-device LLM capability for reliable financial reasoning unproven at 3B-parameter scale for this use case.
Timing risk: several macro items mid-flight as of report date, could shift within a quarter.
